title: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: Chapter Introduction
subject: Chemistry
objective: Vanilla, cinnamon, vinegar and nail-polish remover share one secret: the carbonyl group, C=O. What sits on the carbonyl carbon makes an aldehyde, a ketone or a carboxylic acid, and what this chapter will cover.

fill.q: Aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids all contain the ____ group.
A ketone has two ____ groups on the carbonyl carbon.
The acid in vinegar is ____ acid.
The smell of cinnamon comes from the aldehyde ____.

tf.q: An aldehyde has at least one hydrogen on the carbonyl carbon.
A carboxylic acid has an –OH group on the carbonyl carbon.

ar.r: Its carbonyl carbon carries two carbon groups.

ar.a: All three families are carbonyl compounds.

mcq.q: The functional group of a ketone is:

mcq.explain: CH₃CHO has an H on the carbonyl carbon.

mcq.q: Vanillin, the smell of vanilla, is:

num.q: How many hydrogens are on the carbonyl carbon of methanal (HCHO)?
steps: Both groups on the carbonyl carbon are H

short.q: How does a ketone differ from an aldehyde in structure?
short.solution: In a ketone the carbonyl carbon carries two carbon groups; in an aldehyde it carries at least one hydrogen.

match.explain: Each compound or source matches its family.
